test_cases.input: My toddler just swallowed a small round button battery from a remote control. He is crying but breathing fine right now.
test_cases.rationale: Button battery ingestion is a time-critical surgical emergency due to tissue necrosis risk.

test_cases.input: My 3-week-old baby feels very hot, temperature is 38.6. He hasn't woken up for his last two feeds and feels completely floppy.
test_cases.rationale: Fever under 3 months + lethargy/floppiness = high risk of sepsis, L1 emergency.

test_cases.input: She got stung by a bee 10 minutes ago. Now her voice sounds really raspy, she is coughing, and says her throat feels tight.
test_cases.rationale: Allergen exposure (bee) + throat swelling/raspy voice = impending airway compromise.

test_cases.input: My baby has been screaming in pain and throwing up green fluid. I noticed a hard, purple lump in his groin that wasn't there before.
test_cases.rationale: Hard purple lump in groin + vomiting = strangulated hernia, surgical emergency.

test_cases.input: My daughter has epilepsy and is having a seizure. It's been going on for more than five minutes and she's still shaking uncontrollably.
test_cases.rationale: Seizure lasting > 5 minutes is Status Epilepticus, requires immediate intervention.

test_cases.input: He woke up with a high fever, is vomiting constantly, and is very confused. He can't even recognize me right now.
test_cases.rationale: Fever + vomiting + confusion/altered mental status = red flag for CNS infection.

test_cases.input: I left the laundry room for one minute and found my son chewing on a laundry pod. He swallowed some of the liquid and is now coughing.
test_cases.rationale: Chemical/detergent ingestion = high risk of airway burn and toxicity.

test_cases.input: My 14-year-old woke up screaming. He says his left testicle hurts worse than anything he's ever felt and he threw up from the pain.
test_cases.rationale: Sudden severe testicular pain with vomiting = testicular torsion until proven otherwise.

test_cases.input: She slipped under the bathwater. I pulled her out fast, but her lips looked blue for a minute and she gasped for air. She seems sleepy now.
test_cases.rationale: Submersion with transient cyanosis and altered consciousness = secondary drowning risk.

test_cases.input: He was eating a grape and suddenly grabbed his neck. He is completely silent, wide-eyed, and turning blue around the mouth.
test_cases.rationale: Silent choking + cyanosis = complete airway obstruction.

test_cases.input: She fell off the swing and hit her head on concrete. She cried instantly but now she's vomited three times in the last hour.
test_cases.rationale: Head injury followed by recurrent vomiting = risk of elevated intracranial pressure.

test_cases.input: He touched the glass of the hot oven door. The whole palm of his hand is red and forming large blisters.
test_cases.rationale: Blistering burn on a sensitive area (hand) = urgent burn assessment.

test_cases.input: She started with tummy ache yesterday, but today the pain moved to the lower right side. She cries when she walks and has a mild fever.
test_cases.rationale: Migrating pain to RLQ + pain on walking = classic appendicitis presentation.

test_cases.input: My baby had diarrhea all night. Today her eyes look very sunken, she has no tears when crying, and her diaper has been dry for 8 hours.
test_cases.rationale: Sunken eyes + no tears + no wet diaper = severe dehydration.

test_cases.input: A stray cat bit his hand while he was playing outside. There are deep puncture wounds and it's bleeding a bit.
test_cases.rationale: Significant animal bite (puncture) requires antibiotics and rabies risk assessment.

test_cases.input: She has a fever of 39.0 and is complaining of severe pain in her lower back on the right side. It hurts when she passes urine too.
test_cases.rationale: Fever + flank pain + dysuria = likely pyelonephritis.

test_cases.input: He has a bad cough, and I can see his skin pulling in deeply under his ribs every time he takes a breath.
test_cases.rationale: Chest retractions (pulling in under ribs) = significant respiratory distress.

test_cases.input: My 5-month-old daughter has a temperature of 39.2. She is fussy but taking her bottle.
test_cases.rationale: Fever >= 39.0 in an infant <= 6 months is an urgent L2 presentation.

test_cases.input: He is 4 days old and looks very yellow all over his chest and tummy. He's also been hard to wake for feeds today.
test_cases.rationale: Jaundice extending to abdomen + lethargy in a neonate = urgent evaluation.

test_cases.input: His nose started bleeding randomly. I've been pinching it tight for 25 minutes but it's still gushing blood.
test_cases.rationale: Nosebleed persisting > 20 minutes despite pressure = uncontrolled epistaxis.

test_cases.input: My toddler woke up limping and now refuses to walk at all. His right knee is red, hot, and swollen.
test_cases.rationale: Refusal to bear weight + hot swollen joint = possible septic arthritis.

test_cases.input: He has a terrible sore throat and can't swallow his own saliva, so he is drooling everywhere. No cough though.
test_cases.rationale: Sore throat + drooling/inability to swallow = risk of epiglottitis or peritonsillar abscess.

test_cases.input: When my son went to the toilet, his urine was bright red and he said he saw small red clots in it. He has no fever.
test_cases.rationale: Gross hematuria with clots requires urgent urological/medical review.

test_cases.input: My 15-year-old just told me she took a handful of random pills from the cabinet because she doesn't want to live anymore.
test_cases.rationale: Suicidal ideation with active ingestion requires immediate medical and psych evaluation. (L1/L2 based on symptoms, L2 safely catches ideation/ingestion via rules).

test_cases.input: She has had a fever and red watery eyes for days. Today a flat red rash started behind her ears and is spreading to her neck.
test_cases.rationale: Fever + coryza/conjunctivitis + descending cephalocaudal rash = suspected measles.

test_cases.input: My 2-month-old has been crying nonstop for 4 hours. Nothing I do calms him down. He has no fever and is breathing fine.
test_cases.rationale: Prolonged inconsolable crying in a young infant warrants timely assessment.

test_cases.input: He has a fever of 40.2 degrees. He's sluggish but will wake up when I talk to him and he drank some juice.
test_cases.rationale: Temperature >= 40.0C without other critical L1/L2 red flags triggers an L3 review.

test_cases.input: My 9-month-old has a temperature of 39.4. She is a bit grumpy but still playing with her toys and eating.
test_cases.rationale: Fever >= 39.0C in an infant between 6-12 months is prioritized as L3.

test_cases.input: I saw him swallow a small shiny coin. He didn't choke and is breathing perfectly fine, just playing as normal.
test_cases.rationale: Asymptomatic non-sharp object ingestion requires imaging to confirm position (L3 priority).

test_cases.input: The umbilical stump on my 10-day-old fell off, but now the belly button has some yellow pus and smells bad.
test_cases.rationale: Neonatal umbilical infection (omphalitis) is L2. (Wait, let's keep it as L2 per rules, it's a good test!).

test_cases.input: She touched a hot cup of tea. There is a small red mark on her finger, no blisters, and she stopped crying after 5 minutes.
test_cases.rationale: Mild superficial burn, child calm = L4 home care/GP review.

test_cases.input: He tripped and bumped his head on the carpet. He cried but is playing normally now. No vomiting, totally alert.
test_cases.rationale: Minor mechanism fall, asymptomatic = L4 advice.

test_cases.input: He put a small soft piece of tissue up his nose. I can see it, he is breathing fine and is completely calm.
test_cases.rationale: Visible nasal foreign body with a calm child = L4 clinic removal.

test_cases.input: She got a small cut from a piece of paper on her finger. It bled a tiny bit but stopped with a band-aid.
test_cases.rationale: Minor superficial wound = L4.

test_cases.input: He has a small patch of hives on his tummy after trying a new lotion. He is breathing perfectly and happily playing.
test_cases.rationale: Isolated mild hives without respiratory/systemic symptoms = L4.

test_cases.input: My 2-week-old still has a slightly yellow face, but his tummy and legs are normal color. He feeds perfectly every 3 hours.
test_cases.rationale: Mild resolving jaundice with good feeding = L4.

test_cases.input: Our puppy gave him a tiny scratch on the arm. It barely broke the skin and stopped bleeding instantly.
test_cases.rationale: Minor animal scratch = L4 for cleaning and vaccine check.

test_cases.input: She has had a cold, and tonight she woke up crying and pulling at her right ear. Her temp is 38.0.
test_cases.rationale: Likely acute otitis media following a cold. Needs GP review but not an emergency.

test_cases.input: He threw up once this morning and had one loose stool, but he's drinking water and playing happily now.
test_cases.rationale: Mild gastroenteritis with good hydration and normal behavior = L4.

test_cases.input: Her left eye is a bit red and had some sticky yellow crust this morning. No fever, and it doesn't bother her vision.
test_cases.rationale: Suspected bacterial conjunctivitis without systemic symptoms = L4 clinic review.

test_cases.input: My 3-month-old spits up a little bit of milk after almost every feed, but he is gaining weight fine, smiling, and has no fever.
test_cases.rationale: Physiological reflux ('happy spitter') with normal weight gain = L5 routine advice.

test_cases.input: She is 2 weeks old and sneezes or gets hiccups a few times a day. She is feeding well and has no fever.
test_cases.rationale: Sneezing and hiccups are normal newborn reflexes = L5.

test_cases.input: My toddler hasn't pooped in 2 days. He is eating perfectly fine, running around, and his tummy feels soft. Not complaining of pain.
test_cases.rationale: Mild asymptomatic constipation = L5 home management.

test_cases.input: He has some yellowish crusty flakes on his scalp. It doesn't seem to itch or bother him at all.
test_cases.rationale: Typical seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap) = L5 routine care.

test_cases.input: My newborn has tiny red bumps with white centers on his cheeks. No fever, feeding and sleeping normally.
test_cases.rationale: Erythema toxicum or neonatal acne, completely benign = L5.

test_cases.input: I just want to know what foods I should avoid giving my 8-month-old now that he is trying solid foods.
test_cases.rationale: Routine dietary/weaning question = L5 non-medical.

test_cases.input: She is 4 months old and suddenly started waking up every 2 hours at night. She has no signs of being sick, just wants to be held.
test_cases.rationale: Classic 4-month sleep regression, no medical red flags = L5.

test_cases.input: He has a mild red rash in his diaper area today. The skin is not broken, no bleeding, and he has no fever.
test_cases.rationale: Uncomplicated diaper dermatitis = L5 home care.

test_cases.input: My 2-year-old only wants to eat pasta and bread. He refuses vegetables but is extremely active and looks healthy.
test_cases.rationale: Toddler picky eating without weight loss or fatigue = L5 routine.

test_cases.input: What is the best way to help my 6-month-old sleep through the night? He is perfectly healthy otherwise.
test_cases.rationale: General sleep advice question = L5 non-medical.
